Area.evidence_source: Consolidating our findings from the chart reviews and interviews, we documented a host of adverse factors in our samples of Asian immigrants who repeatedly attempted suicides. In addition to persistent mental illness, these included social isolation, lack of support and acceptance from family, unemployment, feelings of hopelessness, impulsivity, and poor coping during times of distress. [...] Conversely, the apparent link between improved interpersonal relationships and adherence to treatment and higher functioning, as identified among half of our interview sample, pointed to psychological well-being as a protective factor. For those participants, the feelings of being in reciprocally caring relationships and a sense of competency in their life roles appeared to have mitigated their sense of self-loathing and burden on others, improved their coping mechanisms and help-seeking behaviors, and had a bidirectional impact on their motivation to remain in treatment and press for recovery from mental illness.
